title: Angle Stream Heartbeat Payload
description: Liveness only, emitted every HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS whether or not the sensor is streaming, and once immediately on connect. Carries no angle: the last angle is deliberately never repeated as a keepalive, because a stale angle presented as a live one is the one failure a medical readout may not have. A subscriber tells 'the sensor is idle' (heartbeats, no angle) from 'the nav app is gone' (nothing at all) with this frame and HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS.
$comment: The `link` sub-object is repeated verbatim in frame-inclination.json and frame-theta.json rather than $ref'd, so that each payload schema stands alone for a generator and for a firmware-adjacent reader. tests/py/test_schemas.py asserts the three copies are identical, so the duplication cannot drift.

calibrated.description: True once needle-guide has captured a zero-reference vector. False means any angle it reports is measured from an unknown reference.

state.description: needle-guide's SerialPortClient link state, verbatim. Free-form on the guide side: carry it, show it, never branch on it.

live.description: True only for `connected`, i.e. sensor samples are actually flowing.

protocol_version.description: OPTIONAL. The angle-stream wire version the emitter speaks. Rides the heartbeat so liveness and version arrive on the same tick: a subscriber that has a heartbeat has, by construction, everything it needs to decide whether it can read the angle frames. Absent from an emitter built before this field existed, which a subscriber must read as 'unknown', never as 1.

protocol_package_version.description: OPTIONAL. Semver of the needle-protocol package the emitter was built against. Diagnostic, not a compatibility gate -- `protocol_version` is the gate. It exists so an operator staring at two disagreeing screens can tell which side is behind without opening either build.
